thread:
ops-bot: 🚨 ALERT: p99 latency breach on /v1/generate (continuous-batch path) in us-west-2. trending: p95 up 2.5x, p99 up 4x. paging eng-oncall. rule: contbatch-tail-p99 > 700ms.
maya: saw the page, joining. pulling p95/p99 dashboards now.
liam: I can be on-call for this one, handing off to maya if she's already on it.
sam: digging into stream logs, seeing stalls around long-tail KV evictions.
maya: timeline so far — spike started ~1776999900, correlated with a customer traffic burst to streaming endpoints. Streaming requests hitting cont-batch path.
eva: any customer reports yet? support channel quiet but I'll check CS.
liam: quick note: cont-batch scheduling fairness also shows large variance across tenants, some tenants starved then huge pack sizes.
maya: grabbing flamegraphs and batch-size histograms.
ops-bot: automated mitigation suggestion: set `max_batch_size` smaller for cont-batch; enable per-tenant fairshare. recommended: rollback to 32 -> 16 for hot queue.
sam: reproducing locally with mixlen workload — mixed sequence lengths cause pack padding causing oversized batches then paging/KV churn.
maya: log excerpt: ```
2024-12-08T17:05:12Z WARN scheduler: batch_wait 120ms, batch_size=96, effective_seqlen=4096
2024-12-08T17:05:12Z ERROR runtime: kv_evict latency=312ms
```
liam: that `batch_size=96` is way above the steady-state target. we have docs recommending 32/64 depending on seqmix.
sam: streaming stalls show `hold_for_kv` loop spinning while evictions finish; tail requests pile up.
eva: flagged 2 customers who had increased error-rate alerts; outreach queued.
maya: immediate mitigation I can push: lower max_batch_size on us-west-2 cont-batch pool, enable aggressive kv-evict backpressure. prepping a canary.
liam: +1. also toggle `streaming_preempt=true` to prefer streaming paths over big packing for 10m.
sam: config diff I'll apply: ```yaml
cont_batch:
  max_batch_size: 32
  streaming_preempt: true
  kv_evict_backoff_ms: 50
```
maya: planning rollout -> canary 10% on 3 nodes, monitor contbatch_p99 and stream_stall_count.
eva: ETA to notify impacted customers after initial mitigation? prefer to wait 10m and confirm p99 drop.
ops-bot: deployment bot: starting canary on pool contbatch-usw2-rtv-01 (3 nodes). trace-id=abc123.
maya: canary live. watching latency traces.
liam: watching scheduler metrics — fairshare imbalance reduced after canary but KV eviction still spikes on some hosts.
sam: digging host-level: two hosts showing heavy KV churn due to large seqlen-heavy tenants. evict thrash.
maya: next mitigation if canary doesn't land: isolate offending tenant to separate pool (temp route by tenant-id) or enforce per-tenant max_pack_size.
eva: support update prepared: "We observed elevated p99 latency for generation endpoints in us-west-2 impacting streaming; engineering is running mitigations and we'll update in 15m." want me to post now?
maya: hold — wait 5m, confirm canary metrics. if p99 down >50% then post.
ops-bot: canary metrics: contbatch p99 reduced 45%, stream_stall_count down 60% on canary nodes. overall cluster p99 down 20%.
liam: good signal. still seeing 2 hosts with kv_evict latency >200ms. those hosts have older kernel+hugepages settings; I'm rolling a quick host-level cache throttle.
sam: applying temp throttle via `rt_qos` on those hosts to limit eviction IO.
maya: after throttle, cluster p99 down 65% and p95 back within SLO.
eva: support: posting update now. message: "Mitigation in progress; p99 improved significantly; engineering continues root cause work and will provide final RCA." send?
maya: send. include ETA for RCA: 48h.
eva: posted to status page and notified customers flagged earlier.
liam: next steps for postmortem: root cause hypotheses: (1) mixed-seq workload created oversized pack with padding -> larger KV footprint -> eviction thrash; (2) scheduler fairness allowed bursty tenants to monopolize pack slots; (3) host-level memory config exacerbated eviction latency.
sam: data to collect: trace slices for 30m window, batch_size histogram per tenant, kv_eviction latency per host, kernel io stats. I'll export dashboards.
maya: handoff summary for next oncall (liam): mitigations applied: reduced max_batch_size to 32 (cluster), enabled streaming_preempt, kv_evict_backoff set to 50ms, host throttles on two nodes. Canary succeeded. customer notifications sent.
liam: acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring for 2h, then revert host throttles into a proper kernel tuning patch if stable.
eva: CS to follow up with customers who saw errors. thanks team. :clap:
maya: adding todo for postmortem: reproduction script (sim-mixlen-burst), guidance for per-tenant max_pack_size, and scheduler fairness tuning doc.
ops-bot: Incident closed? auto-check in 10m for stability.
liam: closing timeline note: incident opened 1776999900, mitigations started 1777000010, canary green 1777000060, cluster stable by 1777000115.
sam: leaving logs bundle in /var/stack/incidents/1777000001.tar.gz and uploading to incident folder.
maya: thanks all. if anything regresses ping here or escalate to oncall-2.
ops-bot: recorded incident ticket #INC-2024-1777000001. tags: cont-batch, p99, kv-evict, mixedseq, streaming.
